title: Release job build output on every close and refuse starts on low disk
summary: Finished, failed, errored or interrupted job workspaces must drop their cargo target output (clean_job exists but misses some exits), and a job must refuse to start when free disk is below a configured floor. Audience is the operator whose jobs die with "No space left on device".

defaults_applied.how: Tests added; cargo test and clippy criteria.
Criteria exercise cleanup and refusal via tests.
Prefer an existing crate for free-space lookup.
Threshold enforced in code and config, not prose.
All close paths release build output, not just the one that failed.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The leak is in exit paths of run.rs that return without clean_job (e.g. early `return Ok(closing)` failures, errors, interrupts), plus Blocked jobs deliberately kept; I did not trace each exit.
Free-disk detection needs a maintained crate (buy-first) or std-only approach; athena.toml gets a new key only if the threshold is configurable.
Existing stale workspaces on disk are not swept unless a startup sweep is cheap; the main fix is per-job release.

acceptance_criteria.text: A test makes a job end in each of failed, errored (early return), and interrupted states, then asserts the job's work/verify directories, including any target/ build output, no longer exist afterwards. Run `cargo test --locked` and cite the test names.

A test with free disk reported below the configured minimum shows a job is refused before any agent is invoked, with a message naming free and required space; with enough free space the job starts. Run `cargo test --locked` and cite the test names.
The minimum free-disk threshold is configurable (athena.toml, with a documented default) and the refusal message tells the operator what to free or change.
Blocked jobs that must keep their workspace for resume still keep source but drop target/ build output; a test checks this. Run `cargo test --locked`.

Cleanup is best effort: a removal failure never changes a job's outcome, and a low-disk check that cannot read free space does not block the job silently (it warns). Checked by a test via `cargo test --locked`.

out_of_scope: Fixing the plan-pass issues from job 20261016-044847-hem1
Changing the verifier sandbox or its command list
departures: Touches config plus lifecycle paths and possibly a new dependency, so cost and time sit above the reference.
